claims.claim: Cyril of Jerusalem was the bishop (archbishop) of Jerusalem in the mid‑4th century, born around 313 and dying in 386.
He is venerated as a Church Father and Doctor of the Church whose surviving writings include catechetical lectures and homilies.
The Homily on the Paralytic at the Pool (Homilia in paralyticum juxta piscinam jacentem) is a Greek sermon in which Cyril explains the Gospel story of the paralytic at the Pool of Bethesda.
The text survives in the Patrologia Graeca (Migne, vol. 33, column 1132) and has been reproduced in modern editions such as the two‑volume “Works of Saint Cyril of Jerusalem” on the Internet Archive.
